designCoherence.reason: One palette, Fraunces/Instrument/JetBrains Mono and the day arc run through site, portal chart, app dial, scene decal and social set, but the system frays at the edges: the tablet hero (home-tablet.png) has no sun at all, the arc is crisp white dashes on desktop story cards (story-chapter-1.png) but near-invisible hairline dots on phone (home-mobile.png), the app Devices list (app-devices.png) is unstyled while the portal Devices page uses cards and pills, and History is a plain table with no trace of the direction.

brandAlignment.reason: Reads as calm, warm and plain-spoken and avoids both category conventions: warm paper and indigo instead of green-on-black, flat horizons instead of gloss, copy like 'Noon is for storing' and 'kept back, by your choice'. Nothing on the prohibited list appears. Points lost for breaking the brand's own day-arc rules at night (amber sun on the night cover of guidelines.html, grey sun at 21:00 in app-today-evening.png, stars inside the dark headline in home-desktop-dark.png).

visualHierarchy.reason: Desktop web is well paced (big serif statement, mono figure, small plain label in story-chapter-1..4.png). Elsewhere the hierarchy slips: on portal Settings (portal-settings.png) the backup reserve, which the success measure depends on, is a 13px label with no heading; the phone portal chart (portal-mobile.png) shrinks to unreadable; the hero subcopy and CTAs sit on the hill crest (home-desktop.png); the app Devices list is one flat column of text.

typography.reason: Typography is the strongest part. Fraunces statements with tight tracking, Instrument Sans body and every figure in JetBrains Mono with a plain label (22 % / 'left in the Cell at sunrise'). Arabic is set in IBM Plex Sans Arabic at 700 with its own hierarchy, not as fake serif. Weak spots: Arabic eyebrow, stat labels and nav are about 11-13px, under the guideline's own 14px floor; the Arabic hero breaks 'شروق / الشمس' across lines; chart labels on the phone portal are about 5px.

originality.reason: The day arc is a real idea, and it works in the scroll story, as the sun-at-Now marker on the portal chart (portal-desktop.png) and as the app dial with the battery ring (app-today.png). Around those moments the work falls back on stock patterns: the portal is a sidebar, KPI tiles, accordions and a data table; the homepage feature cards use generic contour, rainbow-wave and bell-curve art; the symbol is an arc in a rounded app tile and reads as a cloche or speedometer at 24px.

motionQuality.reason: Not assessed. I reviewed still screenshots and static renders only, so scroll-linked timing, easing, the sun's travel and the reduced-motion crossfade could not be judged. The four story-chapter stills do show coherent keyframes (06:10, 12:40, 18:30, 02:00). The score is a neutral placeholder.

interactionClarity.reason: Good: the portal forecast state has a clear 'Showing 18:30 forecast · Back to now' banner (portal-forecast.png), device states carry icon plus label, and there is 'Show the data as a table'. Unclear: the app's time stepper (app-today-evening.png) uses tiny -/+ glyphs and gives no sign that 21:00 is a replay or forecast; the app reserve uses up/down chevrons on a horizontal slider; app device rows have no tap affordance; the reserve slider mirrors in the Arabic app but not in the Arabic portal.

assetQuality.reason: The social set (og-image, social-square, story, presentation-title PNGs) is cleanly built and follows the arc construction (horizon at about 66%, arc 80% wide). The logo system is complete. The 3D Cell (scene-desktop.png) is a featureless rounded box floating in a soft radial halo, and the Dusk finish renders as saturated ultramarine, not Indigo (scene-finish-2.png). The homepage illustrations are four unrelated styles.

presentationPolish.reason: Desktop web, guidelines and social exports look finished. Visible rough edges: no sun and a cropped arc on the tablet hero; at 1024x768 the hero sun's halo is cut by a hard rectangular notch (own render); the app Devices and device-detail screens look unfinished; the 'Do not outline' misuse tile shows an empty square; client-facing pages carry demo scaffolding ('What we hope people will say', 'Built from one Experience DNA with Creative Intelligence Studio').

professionalReadiness.reason: Not ready to show the client without another pass. Two of the brief's three audiences meet defects on their main device: the tablet hero lacks the signature, the phone portal chart cannot be read at arm's length, and the Arabic social assets do not exist. The portal and app secondary screens still look like a template, and native iOS and Android builds were never run (qa-summary: blocked).

findings.where: web home hero at tablet and small-laptop widths (home-tablet.png, home-ar-tablet.png; confirmed in own renders of web/dist at 768x1024, 834x1194 and 1024x768)
findings.issue: At 768 and 834px the hero picture is a band of hills with the horizon about 20% from the top. The sun is cropped off above the frame and only the two arc legs show as faint dots in the top corners, so the signature is missing from the first screen in both locales. That breaks the guideline's construction rule (horizon at 66%) and its 'large calm sky' composition. At 1024x768 the sun appears, but its outer halo is cut by a hard rectangular notch below-left of the disc (own render), apparently the text-block mask clipping it.
findings.suggestion: Design the tablet hero as its own composition: sky above, horizon in the lower third, sun placed by time. Make the text-block mask clip only the dashed arc, never the sun or its halo. Add 768, 834 and 1024 widths to the QA capture set.

findings.where: day-arc stroke on phone and tablet (home-mobile.png, home-ar-mobile.png and their dark versions, home-tablet.png story cards and hero; brand/applications/png/story.png, social-square.png)
findings.issue: On desktop the story-card arc is a clear white dashed line (story-chapter-1.png). On phone and tablet the same arc is drawn as hairline dots that almost vanish against the sky. In the 06:10 card the sun seems to float with no path, and the phone hero arc is barely visible. The story and square exports have the same hairline arc at feed size. The guideline asks for one dashed arc ('dash one unit, gap about three'); it does not say the stroke may thin out on small formats.
findings.suggestion: Set a minimum on-screen stroke width and dash length for the arc (for example 1.5px stroke, dash 4 / gap 12 at 1x) and scale it per format, not with the viewBox. Re-export the story and square at that weight.

findings.where: portal Today on a phone (portal-mobile.png, portal-mobile-dark.png, portal-ar-mobile.png, portal-ar-mobile-dark.png, chart card)
findings.issue: The 'The day so far' chart is the desktop SVG scaled into about 330x130px. Time labels (00:00, 06:00) and the 'Now' tag are about 4-5px, and the three series blur together. The brief asks for 'readable at arm's length' and the DNA says mobile compositions are designed separately, not scaled down. On the device customers use daily, the signature chart is decoration.
findings.suggestion: Build a phone chart: taller plot, at most four time labels at 12px or more, a thicker arc, the sun-at-Now readout as the main element, and the legend chips folded into the readout row.

findings.where: portal History (portal-history.png, portal-history-mobile.png, portal-history-ar-mobile.png)
findings.issue: History is a paginated admin table with ISO dates (2026-10-31), a free-text filter that asks for 'For example 2026-10', and kWh columns. Nothing of the direction appears: no day arc, no horizon, no curve, although the homepage promises 'The day, drawn as a curve'. It reads like a template, not like Haldora, and dates written as '31 Oct' or 'Yesterday' would match the plain-language voice better.
findings.suggestion: Lead with a visual history, for example a strip of small day arcs or sky tiles per day, coloured by self-powered share and labelled in words. Keep the table as the 'Show as table' alternative. Use friendly dates and a date picker instead of a typed filter.

findings.where: mobile app Devices and device detail (app-devices.png, app-devices-dark.png, app-devices-ar.png, app-device-detail*.png)
findings.issue: The list is a single left-aligned stack of icon tile, name, location and status text: no cards, no dividers, no chevron, and more than half the screen empty. Nothing shows that the rows can be tapped. The detail screen shows only Location and Firmware. The portal's Devices page has cards and status pills with icons, and the app's Today screen has cards, so this screen looks unfinished next to both.
findings.suggestion: Use the same row card as the portal (status pill with icon, chevron, 44pt or larger target) and show what 'Needs attention' means on the row. Give the detail screen useful content (state, last seen, what to do) instead of firmware alone.

findings.where: night and dark-scheme behaviour of the signature (brand/guidelines.html cover; app-today-evening.png; app-today-dark.png; app-web-mobile-dark.png; portal-desktop-dark.png; home-desktop-dark.png hero)
findings.issue: Several places break the guideline's own day-arc rules. The guidelines cover puts an amber sun with a brown halo on a night sky, while the rules say the sun is parchment against night skies and that at night there is no sun above the horizon. At 21:00 the app dial shows a dark grey sun disc on the horizon instead of a crescent or nothing. In the dark scheme the sun on the portal chart, the app dial and onboarding is coral, which is neither amber nor parchment. In the dark web hero, stars sit inside the headline block (between 'energy' and 'from', and beside 'home's'), against 'stars are kept out of it'.
findings.suggestion: Write the night and dark rules into one shared sun component (amber by day, parchment at dawn and dusk, crescent or nothing after sunset) and use it in the app, portal and guidelines. Recolour the guidelines cover. Mask stars out of text blocks.

findings.where: 3D product presentation (scene-desktop.png, scene-finish-2.png, scene-finish-3.png, scene-evening.png, scene-mobile.png)
findings.issue: The Cell is a plain rounded box with a printed arc decal and nothing else. There are no seams, no mounting, and nothing that makes it look like a product rather than a placeholder. It floats in front of the wall inside a soft radial grey halo instead of casting a contact shadow from upper-left light. The floor line is a steep diagonal that fights the near-frontal view of the product. The Dusk finish renders as saturated ultramarine with a bright top-edge highlight, far from Indigo #2A2D66 and close to the 'gloss' the brief rules out. For a launch deliverable this is the weakest piece.
findings.suggestion: Even before industrial design signs off, add believable detail (seam, wall bracket, a status window that holds the arc), ground the product with a contact shadow and a soft directional key light from the upper left, frame the wall and floor so they agree with the camera, and tune the Dusk material (lower saturation, higher roughness) until it reads as matte indigo.

findings.where: portal Settings and Today (portal-settings.png, portal-desktop.png)
findings.issue: Backup reserve is the control in the brief's success measure, but on Settings it is a 13px bold label without a heading, sitting above a long slider that needs 'Save changes'. The Display card below has a Fraunces heading, so the less important setting looks more important. Today has no route to the reserve at all.
findings.suggestion: Give Backup reserve a section heading and a large mono value. Consider saving on release, and add a reserve chip or link to Today, next to 'In the battery'.

findings.where: homepage feature cards, "Clever, and happy to explain itself" (home-desktop.png, home-desktop-dark.png, home-mobile.png)
findings.issue: The four cards use four unrelated illustration styles: topographic contour lines, a saturated stack of amber, iris, ember and fern waves, a bell-curve chart, and no picture at all on 'Less from the grid'. The wave stack breaks 'warm grounds, one deep colour, one bright one'. In the dark scheme the pictures stay on light paper and glare.
findings.suggestion: Draw all four from the approved motifs (arc, horizon, grain) in one style, give the fourth card a picture, and make dark-scheme variants.

findings.where: homepage testimonials and footer (home-desktop.png, home-ar-desktop.png, home-mobile.png)
findings.issue: The section is headed 'What we hope people will say', and the footer reads 'Built from one Experience DNA with Creative Intelligence Studio'. Disclosing that the quotes are fictional is right, but the heading and the vendor credit read as demo scaffolding in a client-facing page. The footer also has no navigation, only a 16px symbol.
findings.suggestion: Keep the fictional-quote disclosure as a small footnote but give the section a brand heading, move the studio credit out of the client footer, and design a proper footer (lockup, links, language switch).

findings.where: Arabic typography details (home-ar-desktop.png hero and story labels, home-ar-mobile.png, product-ar-dark.png, portal-ar-desktop.png chart)
findings.issue: The Arabic eyebrow 'بطارية هالدورا سِل المنزلية', the stat labels under the mono figures, the nav items and the 'مرّر لتتابع اليوم' scroll hint are about 9-13px, under the 14px floor the guidelines set for Arabic. The hero headline breaks as 'طاقة بيتك، / من شروق / الشمس إلى الليل', which splits the phrase 'شروق الشمس' across lines. It looks as though the English three-line rhythm was reused. The 'الآن' tag on the portal chart is about 10px and collides with the Now line.
findings.suggestion: Raise Arabic labels to at least 14px, set Arabic line breaks by hand (for example 'طاقة بيتك، / من شروق الشمس / إلى الليل'), and give the chart tag a background and offset.

findings.where: reserve slider direction in Arabic (portal-settings-ar-mobile-dark.png vs app-settings-ar.png)
findings.issue: In the Arabic portal the reserve slider fills from the left. In the Arabic app it is mirrored and fills from the right. The guideline says only the day arc, charts and time controls keep left-to-right, so the portal slider is wrong and the two surfaces disagree.
findings.suggestion: Mirror the portal's reserve slider in RTL to match the app, and keep only time controls left-to-right.

findings.where: mobile app Today time control (app-today.png, app-today-evening.png, app-today-ar.png)
findings.issue: The '-' and '+' buttons have 8px glyphs. Stepping to 21:00 changes the dial and the figures with no sign that this is a forecast or replay rather than live data. The portal handles the same state with a 'Showing 18:30 forecast · Back to now' banner.
findings.suggestion: Show the same 'Showing 21:00 forecast · Back to now' state in the app, enlarge the glyphs, and make clear that the time label can be tapped.

findings.where: mobile app Settings (app-settings.png, app-settings-dark.png, app-settings-ar-dark.png)
findings.issue: 'Simulate being offline' is a developer control shown in customer settings. In the dark scheme the off-state toggles (dark track on a dark card) almost disappear. The reserve uses up/down chevrons to move a horizontal slider, which is the wrong metaphor.
findings.suggestion: Hide demo controls behind a debug flag, give off-state toggles a visible track border in dark, and use -/+ or left/right steppers that match the slider's direction.

findings.where: web hero composition (home-desktop.png, home-ar-desktop.png, home-desktop-dark.png)
findings.issue: The subcopy and both CTAs sit on the first hill crest, so the text overlaps the horizon, and the large calm sky the imagery spec asks for is crowded by the text column.
findings.suggestion: Lower the horizon a little or move the text block up so subcopy and CTAs sit on clean sky, as in og-image.png.

findings.where: portal Today KPI row (portal-desktop.png, portal-forecast.png, portal-mobile.png)
findings.issue: Identical cards mix instantaneous power ('Used by the home 0.4 kW') with a daily total ('Bought from the grid 3.5 kWh'), while 'Right now' shows Grid 0 kW. Side by side they read as a contradiction. In forecast mode the 3.5 kWh total does not change.
findings.suggestion: Label totals as totals ('Bought from the grid today'), or split 'right now' and 'so far today' into two visibly different groups.

findings.where: portal shell (portal-desktop.png, portal-devices.png, portal-settings.png)
findings.issue: Outside the chart the portal is a standard SaaS shell: sidebar, four pastel KPI tiles, accordions, form cards. The 'Right now' card is a list with tick marks where a simple roof-battery-home-grid flow drawing would have explained the house.
findings.suggestion: Bring one direction device into the shell (a horizon band with the sun at the current time on Today, a one-line serif summary of the day) and turn 'Right now' into a small flow picture.

findings.where: brand guidelines and print applications (brand/guidelines.html Misuse; business-card-back in Applications)
findings.issue: The 'Do not outline' misuse tile shows an empty outlined rounded square with no symbol, so it does not show the misuse it names. The business-card back is the one application with no arc or horizon at all.
findings.suggestion: Draw the outlined symbol in the misuse tile and add a small arc or horizon device to the card back.

findings.where: phone layout details (product-mobile.png, home-mobile.png The Cell; scene-desktop.png and scene-tablet.png finish chips)
findings.issue: Size wraps as '62 × 102 × / 16 cm', leaving the multiplication sign at the end of a line. The finish chips push 'Ember' onto a row of its own in the scene panel and on the phone product card.
findings.suggestion: Keep the dimension on one line (no-wrap, smaller size or a stacked W/H/D layout) and let the chips fit one row or use a segmented control.

findings.where: portal theme toggle and story chapter 4 (portal-desktop-dark.png sidebar footer; story-chapter-4.png)
findings.issue: In the dark portal the theme toggle still shows a moon, while the web header switches to a sun. The 02:00 chapter's time label loses the pill background that 06:10, 12:40 and 18:30 have, and stars show through behind it.
findings.suggestion: Show the target scheme's icon consistently, and keep the time pill on every chapter.

findings.where: logo files (brand/logo/png/lockup-horizontal-1200.png, symbol-512.png, favicon-32.png)
findings.issue: The arc and horizon in the symbol are knock-outs (transparent), so they take on whatever ground the logo sits on. On a mid-grey ground they turn grey. At nav and favicon size the mark reads more like a service bell or a speedometer than a sunrise.
findings.suggestion: Consider filled chalk strokes in the master symbol, or document the knock-out behaviour and the grounds it is allowed on. Test recognition at 16-24px.

findings.where: what works and should be protected (story-chapter-1..4.png, portal-desktop.png chart, app-today.png dial, social-square.png, story.png, home-ar-desktop.png)
findings.issue: The four story chapters are the best expression of the direction: one sun, a dashed arc, sky colour by time, and a mono figure with a plain label. The portal chart puts the sun on the arc at 'Now'. The app dial joins the arc and the battery ring well. The social set follows the construction rules. In Arabic the arc correctly keeps sunrise on the left, and chips, back arrows and pagination mirror correctly.
findings.suggestion: Use these as the reference when fixing the weaker surfaces.

findings.where: native iOS and Android (qa-summary: native-ios and native-android blocked)
findings.issue: All app evidence comes from the web export. I could not check native navigation, the system tab bar or back behaviour, or Arabic shaping on device. The device-detail screen draws its own back arrow, which conflicts with the DNA's platform exceptions if the native build does the same.
findings.suggestion: Capture the app on an iOS simulator and an Android emulator before client review, and use the system navigation bar and back behaviour.

findings.where: earlier review: arc through the hero headline
findings.issue: Fixed. At 1440px the arc now stops at the text block in both locales: in home-desktop.png the left half ends above the eyebrow and the right leg comes down clear of the copy, and home-ar-desktop.png mirrors this. A side effect at 1024x768 is that the mask cuts a rectangular notch in the sun's halo (own render); that is recorded as part of the new tablet-hero finding.

findings.where: earlier review: dark-hero moon over the headline
findings.issue: Fixed. In home-ar-desktop-dark.png the crescent sits at the top of the arc, well clear of 'طاقة بيتك'. On home-mobile-dark.png and home-ar-mobile-dark.png it is centred in the picture band above the headline and not cropped. Stars inside the English dark headline block remain (new finding).

findings.where: earlier review: night state of the signature
findings.issue: Fixed for the places listed: the dark hero, the phone and tablet 02:00 story cards and presentation-title.png all use a pale crescent now. The night rule is still broken elsewhere (amber sun on the guidelines cover, grey sun at 21:00 in the app, coral sun in the dark scheme), which is recorded as a new finding.

findings.where: earlier review: app tab bar labels cut off
findings.issue: Fixed. In app-today.png, app-devices.png, app-settings.png and their dark and Arabic versions, tab icons and labels sit fully inside the bar with clear space below. Native rendering is still unverified.

findings.where: earlier review: Arabic app content left in English
findings.issue: Fixed. app-devices-ar.png now shows translated locations and types (المرآب، لوحة الكهرباء، شاحن السيارة، ممر السيارة، محوّل الألواح، العلّية) with product names in Latin, and on app-device-detail-ar.png the back arrow sits on the right and points right.

findings.where: earlier review: guidelines application previews show wrong artwork
findings.issue: Fixed (own render of brand/guidelines.html at 1440px). The og-image preview now shows the pale paper sky and presentation-title the night scene, both matching the exported PNGs. The social-square and story previews also match.

findings.where: earlier review: portal chart unreadable on a phone
findings.issue: Not fixed. portal-mobile.png and portal-ar-mobile.png still show the desktop chart scaled to about 330px wide, with time labels and the 'Now' tag around 4-5px. Recorded again as a new major finding.

findings.where: earlier review: portal shell reads as a stock admin template
findings.issue: Not fixed. portal-desktop.png, portal-devices.png, portal-history.png and portal-settings.png keep the same sidebar, KPI tiles, accordion rows, data table and form cards. No horizon band or serif day summary was added, and History is still only a table.

findings.where: earlier review: brand applications English only
findings.issue: Not fixed. brand/applications/png still contains only English og-image, social-square, story and presentation-title, all with the same headline. There is no Arabic story, square or OG image for the Gulf audience.
